title: Population Genetics I: Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium
objectives: State the five assumptions of Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium (HWE)
Apply the HWE equation to calculate allele and genotype frequencies
Identify factors that disrupt HWE in human populations
Interpret HWE deviations in disease association studies

hwe_fundamentals.title: Core Principles
hwe_fundamentals.content:
HWE Equation
p2 + 2pq + q2 = 1
• p = dominant allele frequency
• q = recessive allele frequency
• p + q = 1
  • No mutations
  • Random mating
  • No natural selection
  • Large population
  • No gene flow

clinical_applications.title: Medical Relevance
clinical_applications.content:
Carrier Frequency Estimation

For cystic fibrosis (q2 = 1/2500):
• q = √(1/2500) = 0.02
• Carrier frequency (2pq) ≈ 2(0.98)(0.02) = 3.9%

Founder Effects

Example: Ellis-van Creveld syndrome in Amish
• q increased due to small founding population
• Observed > expected homozygous affected

hwe_deviations.title: Violations of HWE
hwe_deviations.content:
ViolationEffectClinical Example
Selection↑/↓ specific genotypesSickle cell heterozygote advantage
Non-random mating↑homozygotesConsanguinity → recessive disorders
Genetic driftRandom allele changesTay-Sachs in Ashkenazi Jews

case_studies.title: Problem Solving
case_studies.content:
Scenario: 9% of a population has albinism (autosomal recessive)
Question: What percentage are carriers?
Solution:
• q2 = 0.09 → q = 0.3
• p = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7
• 2pq = 2(0.7)(0.3) = 42% carriers

genetic_testing.title: HWE in NGS Quality Control
genetic_testing.content:
• Variant filtering: HWE p-value < 0.05 flags potential errors
  • Population stratification: Different subpopulations cause false deviations
  • Database references: gnomAD uses HWE for variant annotation

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why does HWE assume an infinitely large population?

To eliminate genetic drift - in small populations, random fluctuations disproportionately affect allele frequencies (e.g., founder effects).

How can sickle cell trait be both protective and violate HWE?

Balancing selection: heterozygote advantage (malaria resistance) maintains both alleles despite negative selection against homozygotes.

Why test HWE in GWAS studies?

Deviations may indicate genotyping errors, population substructure, or true biological selection - critical for distinguishing real associations.
